sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Election 2026: Musk Leads $16 Billion in PAC Spending
cards.content: In the 2026 election cycle, over $16 billion has been raised, with most of it coming from political action committees. Billionaire Elon Musk is expected to be the largest spender, with over $400 million contributed so far. Other big spenders include George Soros and Michael Bloomberg, who have donated tens of millions of dollars to Democratic candidates. Meanwhile, Republican majorities are being bolstered by spending from super PACs and individual donors, with SLF raising over $540 million. As the election approaches, the total amount spent by individual donors and PACs will continue to grow, making it difficult to track the true impact of campaign spending.

cards.title: Kristi Noem Ends Tenure as Shield of Americas Envoy, Confusion Ensues
cards.content: Kristi Noem, former special envoy to the Shield of Americas, posted an official-looking statement on her social media accounts announcing the end of her tenure, but sources claim it was not an official State Department statement. The statement's letterhead appeared to be genuine, but officials say no one on the seventh floor or in the press office saw the memo before it was posted. The substance of the statement was accurate, but the format and apparent authorization by leadership or the press office were not. Noem has since moved into a senior adviser role and is continuing to work on the Shield of the Americas portfolio. A State Department official confirmed that Noem remains at the department as a senior adviser, and the work she's doing with the coalition is being praised by President Donald Trump.

cards.title: Trump Makes Controversial Offers to Voters
cards.content: President Donald Trump has been making voters a series of highly controversial offers, threatening to withhold aid and funding if they don't vote for Republicans. At the Republican midterm convention, Trump initially offered every US adult $5,000 if Republicans keep the majority. Since then, he has offered more targeted deals to voters in about half of the states holding key Senate contests, often framing them as jokes. However, many of these promises are not just humorous, and Trump could deliver on them if he wanted to. The president has linked disaster relief to voting for Republican Michael Whatley, promised to invest $100 million in a drug manufacturing facility in Kentucky if Republicans win, and offered to make E15 fuel available permanently if Roger Marshall wins in Kansas. Trump has also threatened to withhold Department of Justice settlements for water contamination at Camp Lejeune if Republicans don't win. The president's quid pro quos have been met with widespread criticism, with polls showing most voters think the offers are inappropriate and would make them less likely to vote for a candidate who supports Trump's ideas.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: SoftBank to invest $50 billion in Malaysia for AI and tech
cards.content: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that SoftBank Group plans to invest $50 billion in the country, focusing on artificial intelligence, new technologies, and data centers. This planned investment comes as Malaysia aims to become an 'AI nation' by 2030 and follows the government's launch of a national AI action plan. SoftBank's planned investment is part of a growing trend, with Google, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft also investing in the country. Malaysia has already seen $94 billion in data center-related investments between 2021 and the first half of 2026, and the country is seeking to strengthen its AI capabilities and infrastructure. }

cards.title: Musk Warns 200+ Neoclouds at Risk of Collapse Over Debt and Profit Concerns
cards.content: Elon Musk warned that more than 200 companies providing cloud computing services, known as neoclouds, could collapse due to debt issues and concerns over their ability to generate profits. Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, said that debt markets have shut off access to money for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. This could lead to a wave of consolidation and some neoclouds going out of business. Musk's comments came after Chamath Palihapitiya, founder of Social Capital, expressed similar concerns about the data center buildout. The warning comes as neocloud stocks have been falling sharply over the past month, with some companies down by as much as 40%. Nvidia, a major investor in neoclouds, has expressed confidence in the sector's growth potential, but many investors remain jittery. Neocloud executives are defending their companies' demand, saying that customers are still clamoring for their services.

cards.title: AI Takes Over Customer Service, Leaving Humans Dealing with Complex Issues
cards.content: As companies increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to handle customer service, the lives of human customer service representatives are undergoing significant changes. For some, like Kaylee Harris, AI has allowed them to focus more on each customer, while for others, like Shannon, AI-generated notes have led to errors and more work. The automation of routine tasks is meant to free up human agents to handle more complex cases, but some experts warn that this could lead to increased workloads and pressure on employees, potentially causing burnout. As AI takes on more responsibilities, human customer service representatives may be left dealing with a greater share of complicated cases, and the pressure on them comes amid reports of rising workloads across the industry. Experts caution that the push to automate could result in a loss of opportunities for employees to develop the experience needed for more demanding work.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Schizophrenia Linked to Weaker Brain Rhythm
cards.content: A new study published in Science Advances has discovered that changes in brain activity, specifically in a rhythm called beta-band activity, are linked to several symptoms of schizophrenia. Researchers found that patients with schizophrenia showed weaker and slower beta-band activity compared to healthy participants, which was associated with difficulties in processing sensory information, disorganized speech, and severe clinical symptoms. The study suggests that this common disruption in brain activity may be connected to the development of schizophrenia symptoms, including those related to perception, behavior, and speech. The findings could potentially lead to new methods for identifying and supporting individuals at risk of developing psychosis, and even serve as a target for future treatments.

cards.title: Scientists uncover clues to deadly Brazilian virus evolution
cards.content: Scientists have uncovered new clues about the evolution of a rare and deadly Brazilian virus, the Sabiá virus, which has circulated undetected for over a century. Genetic changes allowed the virus to escape existing laboratory tests, leading to the development of an improved detection method. Researchers found that the virus has been circulating in Brazil for approximately 142 years, with likely additional cases going undiagnosed. The study highlights the importance of genomic surveillance in detecting public health risks, particularly in cases where targeted diagnostic tests fail.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: IPCC fails to agree on climate reports timeline
cards.content: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has failed for the sixth consecutive time to agree on a timeline for its Seventh Assessment Cycle reports. The Least Developed Countries are worried that further delays could hinder crucial climate science from informing the second Global Stocktake under the Paris Agreement in 2028. Meanwhile, some countries, including India, Saudi Arabia, and Russia, are pushing for the publication of two major reports in 2029 due to concerns over scientific rigor and inclusivity. The IPCC's 65th plenary session in Ethiopia was suspended without an agreement on the publication schedule or budget. This has left the timeline for publishing three Working Group reports unclear, as countries disagree on the pace of the assessment process. The reports cover climate change's physical science, impacts, and mitigation, which are crucial for informing global climate action.

cards.title: Antarctica Turns Green and Red Due to Penguin Droppings Fueling Algae
cards.content: Antarctica, known for its vast expanses of white ice and snow-covered mountains, is unexpectedly turning green and red in some areas. This phenomenon has caught the attention of scientists who are trying to understand the connection to climate change. One factor contributing to the colorful patches is penguin droppings, which provide nutrients to microscopic algae growing on the snow. The scientists suspect that this natural process may accelerate local melting, adding to the effects of a warming climate. The impact of penguin droppings on the melting of Antarctica's snow is still being studied, and the effects are not yet fully understood.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Wicker Husband Story Becomes Film with Raunchy Twist
cards.content: An author named Ursula Wills wrote a short story, The Wicker Husband, after seeing wicker sculptures on a camping trip. The story follows an ostracized fisherwoman who pays a basket-maker to weave her a husband. The story gained interest online and was later developed into a film, Wicker, starring Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, and Peter Dinklage. The author, who was initially surprised by the film's raunchy content, thinks audiences will go crazy for it. The film, which opens in UK cinemas on October 30, has garnered attention online and spawned viral posts.

cards.title: Spotify Corrects Error in Welsh Version of Dolly Parton's Jolene
cards.content: A Welsh version of Dolly Parton's hit song Jolene, featuring Bronwen Lewis and Jada Star, was mistakenly uploaded to Spotify with Irish lyrics. The song, recorded before Parton's death, features parts in English and Welsh, but the lyrics on Spotify showed it as Irish. After the BBC approached Spotify for comment, the error was removed. This is the second posthumous release from Parton, who was of Welsh descent and won 10 Grammy awards. Jolene, released in 1973, is about the fear of losing her husband to another woman, and it has had over one billion streams on Spotify. The Welsh version of the song was translated by Lewis and recorded with Parton's niece Star, and it follows Parton's revelation of her Welsh ancestry during a 2008 concert in Cardiff.

cards.title: Marzamemi Festival Applies to Hold Family-Friendly Event on Richmond Green
cards.content: A family-friendly Italian-themed festival, the Marzamemi Festival, has applied to hold a three-day event on Richmond Green in south-west London in June. The event, which features live music, food, and activities for children, has received some support but also 45 objections from residents who are concerned about noise and restricted access to the park. The Richmond Society has objected to the event, citing concerns that it will take away public access to a large area of the green, potentially constituting a public nuisance. The event's founder, Emily Ceraudo, describes it as a 'boutique, family-friendly celebration' that aims to support local businesses. The Richmond Council's licensing committee will make a decision on the event in the coming days.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: £20m Refurbishment Plan Proposed for World's End Estate
cards.content: Kensington and Chelsea Council has proposed a £20m refurbishment plan for the World's End Estate in west London. The project, set to start in 2028, will replace some kitchens and bathrooms, renew roofs, and redecorate communal areas. Leaseholders will contribute to the repairs, with tailored support for those most affected. The upgrade includes electrical and fire safety improvements, and a new heat network system to comply with Ofgem regulations. The report notes that upgrading the existing system will require significant investment, which may generate leaseholder recharges. The £20m investment aims to improve homes, enhance resident safety, and secure the estate's future for decades to come.

cards.title: Naomi Nomi Revolutionizes Fashion with Quality, Long-Lasting Clothing
cards.content: Naomi Mishkin, the founder of Naomi Nomi, is revolutionizing the fashion industry by producing high-quality, long-lasting clothing at a higher price point. The average customer starts with one shirt and returns for three more within six months, as they realize the value of her products. Mishkin's approach is a departure from the fast fashion industry, which has mastered the art of cutting production costs to the bone. She uses cotton and wool, making her shirts pricier than fast fashion, but lasting longer. Naomi Nomi's success is attributed to the growing backlash against companies that prioritize profit over quality and the environment. The fashion industry has undergone significant changes over the past few decades, with a shift towards planned obsolescence and the use of cheaper materials. However, some consumers are now looking for brands that offer quality, durability, and sustainability, and Naomi Nomi is capitalizing on this trend.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
